translationRepairs: As superintendent of the grain bureau, he supplied provisions for garrison troops and inter-provincial relief subsidies.
As superintendent of the grain bureau, he supplied provisions for garrison troops and inter-provincial military assistance funds.
他省協餉 is inter-provincial military assistance (xiang), not disaster-relief subsidies; the original invents relief.
At that time the capital region suffered great flooding; Zonglian directed relief affairs and was granted discretionary authority to disburse silk funds and grain.
At that time the capital region suffered great flooding; Zonglian directed relief affairs and was granted discretionary authority to disburse cash-strings and grain.
發緡粟 disburses cash-strings (緡) and grain; silk is a mistranslation of 緡.

In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu (1900), when the allied armies attacked Tianjin, he led Luzhou militia onto the walls in a stubborn defense. A shell splinter shattered his left shin and blood pooled around him, yet he bandaged the wound and kept command.

In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu (1900), when the allied armies attacked Tianjin, he led Changlu militia onto the walls in a stubborn defense. A shell splinter shattered his left shin and blood pooled around him, yet he bandaged the wound and kept command.
蘆勇 here follows 長蘆鹽運使 and are Changlu braves, not Luzhou (廬州) militia.

In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies attacked Tianjin; Zonglian directed Luzhou braves to mount the walls and hold firm; a flying projectile shattered his left shin and blood flowed like a deep pool, yet he still bound his wound and directed the army.

In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies attacked Tianjin; Zonglian directed Changlu braves to mount the walls and hold firm; a flying projectile shattered his left shin and blood flowed like a deep pool, yet he still bound his wound and directed the army.
The same 蘆勇 are Changlu salt-administration braves; Luzhou is the wrong place-name.
Promoted to prefect of Luoding, he stayed in the provincial capital to round up the notorious bandit Liu Yacai and nine hundred accomplices, all of whom were punished under law.
Promoted to department magistrate of Luoding, he stayed in the provincial capital to round up the notorious bandit Liu Yacai and nine hundred accomplices, all of whom were punished under law.
晉羅定知州 is promotion to department magistrate; 知府 comes only later (擢知府).

When rebels arrived in force, Regional Commander Kun Shou advanced by land and water, fought a major battle at the mouth of the Fengchuan River, won successive victories that destroyed the rebel force, and recovered Wuzhou.

When rebels later arrived in force, Regional Commander Kun Shou advanced by land and water together with him; they fought a major battle at the mouth of the Fengchuan River, won successive victories that destroyed the rebel force, and recovered Wuzhou.
會提督昆壽水陸並進 joins Kun Shou to Pu’s continuing campaign; the original makes Kun Shou the sole commander of the Wuzhou recovery.
In the fourth year he died.
In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.
四年 continues 光緒二年 in the preceding sentence and is Guangxu 4, not an unidentified fourth year.
His father Yao Jun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.
His father Yaoyun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.
父燿鋆 is the two-character given name Yaoyun, not the split English name Yao Jun.
His father Yao Jun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.
His father Yaoyun was a subprefect in Hubei; when Wuchang fell he cursed the rebels and was killed.
The literal field repeats the same split of 燿鋆; Yaoyun is the correct given-name romanization.

Hongzhang specially entrusted him with acting as Tianjin customs intendant; three days later he died; an edict granted generous condolence and posthumously awarded Grand Secretariat Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

Hongzhang specially entrusted him with acting as Tianjin customs intendant; three days later he died; an edict granted generous condolence and posthumously awarded him as Chamberlain of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
贈光祿寺卿 is the Guanglu-si chamberlain, not a Grand Secretariat (內閣) vice-minister.
In the twentieth year of Guangxu (1894) he was transferred from Fenghuang to be prefect of Liaoyang.
In the twentieth year of Guangxu (1894) he was transferred from Fenghuang subprefecture to be department magistrate of Liaoyang.
遼陽知州 is a department magistracy, not a prefecture (知府); 鳳凰廳 is a subprefecture.
In the twentieth year of Guangxu he was transferred from Fenghuang subprefecture to be prefect of Liaoyang.
In the twentieth year of Guangxu he was transferred from Fenghuang subprefecture to be department magistrate of Liaoyang.
The literal English likewise upgrades 知州 to prefect; the Chinese names a department magistrate.

After Qingzhang assigned him as drill leader, commanders of regular troops grew jealous and ordered the militia dispersed; coastal defense then slackened, yet the name of the Jidongyu village militia became renowned at home and abroad.

After Qingzhang assigned him as drill leader, commanders of regular troops grew jealous and ordered the militia dispersed; defense then slackened, yet the name of the Jidongyu village militia became renowned at home and abroad.
防務遂弛 is slackening of defense at inland Jidongyu; 防務 does not mean coastal defense.
When war broke out in the Middle East he wrote in indignation to the throne; receiving no response, he requested leave and returned home.
When the Sino-Japanese War broke out he wrote in indignation to the throne; receiving no response, he requested leave and returned home.
中東兵起 in this late-Qing context is the Sino-Japanese War, not a Middle Eastern conflict.

Once Guangdian took office, he stationed steamships at three key points on the great river—first Jiao and Jin, next Sanjiang Mouth, next Shamanzhou—supported by armed boats, and private salt smugglers withdrew.

Once Guangdian took office, he stationed steamships at three key points on the great river—first Jin and Jiao, next Sanjiang Mouth, next Shamanzhou—supported by armed boats, and private salt smugglers withdrew.
首金、焦 names Jin first, then Jiao; the original reverses that order.
When Baoying famine victims looted grain, he quietly had them dispersed.
When Baoying famine victims looted grain, the magistrate secretly fled.
令潛逃 is the county magistrate absconding, not Guangdian quietly dispersing the crowd (that is the next sentence).
Baoying famine victims looted grain; he ordered them to flee secretly.
Baoying famine victims looted grain; the magistrate secretly fled.
令 is the magistrate and 潛逃 is flight; the original treats 令 as ‘ordered them to flee.’
Every October gamblers from Wu and Yue gathered; a single throw could cost thousands of cash and ruin countless families.
Every October gamblers from Wu and Yue gathered; a single throw could cost thousands of taels and ruin countless families.
一擲累千金 is a large metallic stake (gold/taels), not copper cash.

In the nineteenth year he relieved Fengzhen and other banners beyond Datong using the Woniushan model, then entered Shandong service as subprefect, acted in En county, filled Pingdu, and rose to prefect of Tai'an.

In the nineteenth year he relieved Fengzhen and other subprefectures beyond Datong using the Woniushan model, then entered Shandong service as subprefect, acted in En county, filled Pingdu, and rose to prefect of Tai'an.
豐鎮諸廳 are subprefectural tings, not Mongol banners (旗).
In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he was appointed instructor of Andong county as a tribute student.
In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he was appointed instructor of Andong county as a tribute student by grace.
以恩貢授 names a grace tribute student (恩貢); dropping 恩 understates the credential.
When Huai, Xu, and Hai were flooded he poled a small boat through the waters on relief work until his hair turned white from strain.
When Huai, Xu, and Hai were flooded he poled a small boat through the waters on relief work until his beard and hair turned white from strain.
鬚髮為白 names both beard and hair; the original keeps only hair.

In the twenty-sixth year the two palaces went west on hunt; Guanzhong suffered great famine and men ate one another; Xijin collected four hundred thousand taels and went to relieve, passing through two prefectures and eight counties, hardships not slightly hindering him.

In the twenty-sixth year the two palaces fled west; Guanzhong suffered great famine and men ate one another; Xijin collected four hundred thousand taels and went to relieve, passing through two prefectures and eight counties, hardships not slightly hindering him.
兩宮西狩 is the 1900 court flight, a conventional euphemism, not an actual western hunt.
Governor-General Duan Fang had his office restored and reassigned him to Changzhou; later he was promoted to circuit intendant for contributing to relief.
Governor-General Duan Fang and others had his office restored and reassigned him to Changzhou county; later he was promoted to circuit intendant for contributing to relief.
端方等 is Duan Fang and others, and 長洲 is Changzhou county (not 常州 prefecture).
Though he sought no promotion and did not hold office himself, his counsel on governance and people's welfare was the standard for every prefecture and county.
Though he sought no promotion and did not personally administer local government, his counsel on governance and people's welfare was the standard for every prefecture and county.
未親吏治 means he did not personally administer local government, not that he held no office.
